newsitem.title: UK: Iraq says Feb output fell 50,000 bpd to 1.29 mbpd.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Feb output fell 50,000 bpd to 1.29 mbpd.

text.p: Iraq on Tuesday said it pumped 1.29 million barrels a day (bpd) of crude in February, down 50,000 bpd from 1.34 million in January, the OPEC news agency reported.
The data was provided in a monthly submission to OPEC headquarters in Vienna.
Iraqi output has been boosted since December by restricted sales under the U.N.'s oil-for-food exchange.
Prior to the oil sale Baghdad said it was pumping 725,000 bpd for domestic consumption and small volumes for sale to Jordan.
Assuming domestic consumption and Jordanian sales remained unchanged then Iraqi exports in February were 565,000 bpd down from 615,000 bpd in January.
By Tuesday, 10 of OPEC's 11 member countries had submitted some supply and output data for February.
Supply as defined by OPEC, is calculated as domestic consumption, plus net export sales of crude and products, plus withdrawals of stocks held outside national boundaries.
